newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Three Hutu rebels killed in Burundi, army says.
newsitem.headline: Three Hutu rebels killed in Burundi, army says.

text.p: Burundian troops killed three Hutu rebels in a clash in the northwestern province of Cibitoke linked to fighting in eastern Zaire, an army spokesman said on Thursday.
The clash at Masha commune on Wednesday followed the killing of Cibitoke Governor Lieutenant-Colonel Marcel Senarenze along with six bodyguards in an ambush on the province's main road on Tuesday.
"Three assailants (rebels) were killed on Wednesday at Masha during an exchange of fire. There has been fighting in Cibitoke all week," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi.
He gave no details and independent confirmation was impossible because all foreigners have pulled out of Cibitoke.
The body of the killed governor, recovered a day after the ambush, would be buried later on Thursday, Nibizi added.
Diplomats and sources in Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army say a surge in fighting in Cibitoke is a spillover from conflict in east Zaire between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge.
Armed Burundian Hutus, driven east across the Ruzizi river into Burundi from refugee camps north of the Zairean city of Uvira, are stepping up attacks in Cibitoke, a western diplomat said.
The province has seen the worst fighting in a civil war and massacres that have killed 150,000 people in three years.
Burundi, like neighbouring Rwanda which has the same ethnic mix of a Tutsi minority and Hutu majority, have both denied Zairean accusations that their troops are fighting in eastern Zaire.
